headline: Residents evacuated after brick façade collapses on Chelsea building
dek: Fire officials say a large section of the Orange Street building’s front wall failed Sunday night, leaving residents displaced while inspectors assess whether the structure could collapse further.
body: Residents were evacuated from a residential building in Chelsea on Sunday night after a large section of its brick front wall collapsed onto the sidewalk, creating a continuing structural hazard on Orange Street. No injuries were reported, but fire officials said the building was unstable enough that people could not remain inside while crews and inspectors evaluated the damage. [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/chelsea-firefighters-investigating-partial-building-collapse/4FUDDJRTGJAZZFRVRBFC6XYJJY/?outputType=amp) reported that the failure happened Sunday night and that the building’s occupants were sheltered in an MBTA bus during the response.

The collapse involved a large section of the front exterior of a multi-story brick building, according to Chelsea Fire Chief John Quatieri as quoted by Boston 25. [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/chelsea-building-at-risk-of-collapsing-after-exterior-bricks-fall/74104113) described the structure as a three-story building and said dozens of bricks fell from the wall above a second-floor window. The debris landed on the sidewalk below, turning a routine residential entrance into a collapse zone and prompting crews to keep people away from the façade.

The immediate response focused on protecting occupants and limiting additional hazards. [WHDH](https://whdh.com/news/people-evacuate-after-partial-building-collapse-in-chelsea/) reported that firefighters were working in the rain to evaluate the building, while the department prepared to shut off gas and electricity and relocate the occupants. WCVB said residents from two buildings were safely evacuated and sheltered on an MBTA bus. The accounts do not identify how many people were displaced or where they would stay after the emergency sheltering period.

Chelsea’s fire department used its drone unit to inspect parts of the building that were difficult or unsafe to view from the ground. Fire officials told the broadcasters that the aerial view helped crews examine the roof and the sides of the structure while building inspectors assessed its stability. Boston 25 reported that the drone was assisting the inspector; WCVB said the department used it to make decisions about the risk of a further collapse.

The cause of the wall failure had not been established in the initial reports. None of the three accounts reported a fire, an explosion or injuries connected to the collapse, and officials had not announced whether weather, age, maintenance or another factor played a role. That leaves the building’s condition, rather than a confirmed cause, as the central unresolved issue for residents and the city’s inspectors.

Orange Street was closed for several hours while the scene was examined and debris and safety concerns were addressed. [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/residents-evacuated-when-brick-wall-of-building-collapses-in-chelsea/4029470/) reported that the street had reopened to traffic by about 6:30 a.m. Monday, although the building itself remained off-limits because officials were still concerned that more of the structure could fail.

For the displaced residents, the next steps depend on the inspection and any stabilization work required before reentry can be considered. Fire officials had not said when the building might be safe, whether residents could retrieve belongings, or whether neighboring properties would need additional restrictions. Until those questions are answered, the incident remains both a housing disruption and a public-safety investigation centered on a damaged façade above a Chelsea sidewalk.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Chelsea residents evacuated after Orange Street building collapse
seoDescription: Residents were evacuated after a brick façade collapsed on a Chelsea building. Fire officials and inspectors are assessing the structure.
